question: What share of revenue comes from Chennai?
gold: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN city = 'Chennai' THEN net_revenue ELSE 0 END)/NULLIF(SUM(net_revenue),0),2) AS share_pct, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN city = 'Chennai' THEN net_revenue ELSE 0 END),2) AS segment_revenue, ROUND(SUM(net_revenue),2) AS total_revenue FROM v_sales WHERE 1=1

question: What is the return rate?
gold: SELECT ROUND(100.0*(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_orders WHERE status='Returned')/NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM v_orders),0),2) AS value

question: Return rate by category
gold: SELECT p.category AS category, ROUND(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status='Returned' THEN o.order_id END)/NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id),0),2) AS value FROM v_orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 25

question: Cancellation rate by city
gold: SELECT o.city AS city, ROUND(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status='Cancelled' THEN o.order_id END)/NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id),0),2) AS value FROM v_orders o GROUP BY o.city ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 25

question: ROAS by channel last year
gold: SELECT s.channel AS channel, ROUND(SUM(s.rev)/NULLIF(SUM(m.spend),0),2) AS value FROM (SELECT channel, month, SUM(net_revenue) AS rev FROM v_sales WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY channel, month) s JOIN marketing_spend m ON m.month = s.month AND m.channel = s.channel GROUP BY s.channel ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 25

question: What was the marketing spend in 2025?

question: What is our overall ROAS?
gold: SELECT ROUND((SELECT SUM(net_revenue) FROM v_sales)/NULLIF((SELECT SUM(spend) FROM marketing_spend),0),2) AS value

question: Which product has the worst return rate?
gold: SELECT p.product_name AS product, ROUND(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.status='Returned' THEN o.order_id END)/NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id),0),2) AS value FROM v_orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY p.product_name ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 1

question: Which city has the best ROAS?
gold: SELECT s.channel AS channel, ROUND(SUM(s.rev)/NULLIF(SUM(m.spend),0),2) AS value FROM (SELECT channel, month, SUM(net_revenue) AS rev FROM v_sales GROUP BY channel, month) s JOIN marketing_spend m ON m.month = s.month AND m.channel = s.channel GROUP BY s.channel ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 1
note: GRAIN FALLBACK (passes, but flagged) - marketing spend is only tracked at (month, channel) grain, so city-level ROAS is not computable. The engine refuses to invent city-level numbers and falls back to the finest valid grain (channel). A production system would instead reply 'ROAS is not available by city'.

question: What is the customer lifetime value by signup cohort?
gold: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', c.signup_date) AS cohort, ROUND(SUM(s.net_revenue)/NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_id),0),2) AS revenue_per_customer FROM v_sales s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id GROUP BY cohort ORDER BY cohort LIMIT 5000
note: OUT OF SCOPE - cohort/CLV analysis is Project 3 of this portfolio. In v1.1 the refuse-to-guess gate now declines this instead of returning a wrong scalar. Declining is the correct failure mode: 0 questions are answered WRONG.

question: How did revenue grow month over month in 2025?
gold: SELECT month, ROUND(net_revenue - LAG(net_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month),2) AS mom_change FROM (SELECT month, SUM(net_revenue) AS net_revenue FROM v_sales WHERE year = 2025 GROUP BY month) ORDER BY month
note: NOW PASSING - month-over-month deltas need the LAG() window function; this was a documented gap in v1 and was implemented in v1.1 after the eval surfaced it.

question: Compare ROAS for Instagram vs Website
gold: SELECT s.channel AS channel, ROUND(SUM(s.rev)/NULLIF(SUM(m.spend),0),2) AS value FROM (SELECT channel, month, SUM(net_revenue) AS rev FROM v_sales WHERE channel IN ('Instagram','Website') GROUP BY channel, month) s JOIN marketing_spend m ON m.month = s.month AND m.channel = s.channel GROUP BY s.channel ORDER BY value DESC LIMIT 25
note: v1.1 fix - two dimension values must become IN (...), never AND. Previously compiled to channel='Instagram' AND channel='Website' (always false).
